# Combining With the Third Law: Conservation of Momentum

<!-- STEP id="equal-and-opposite" -->
Newton's third law says these two forces are equal in size, opposite in direction:

$$F_{\text{on A}} = -F_{\text{on B}}$$

<!-- STEP id="substitute" -->
$$\frac{m_1(v_1-u_1)}{t} = -\frac{m_2(v_2-u_2)}{t}$$

<!-- STEP id="cancel-t" -->
Both sides share the same collision time t. Multiply through by t and it cancels completely:

$$m_1(v_1-u_1) = -m_2(v_2-u_2)$$

<!-- STEP id="expand" -->
Expand both sides:

$$m_1v_1 - m_1u_1 = -m_2v_2 + m_2u_2$$

<!-- STEP id="rearrange" -->
Gather the "before" terms on one side, the "after" terms on the other:

$$m_1u_1 + m_2u_2 = m_1v_1 + m_2v_2$$

<!-- STEP id="name-the-result" -->
**Total momentum before the collision equals total momentum after.** This is the law of conservation of momentum — and notice it isn't a separate assumption bolted on. It falls straight out of Newton's second and third laws, combined.
